matched_rules.because: Signals show extraordinarily high outside temperatures and an issue affecting two cooling systems, consistent with a cooling-plant threat; however, the signals do not explicitly state storms are active or that a utility-to-generator transfer has occurred, so the rule's 'when' conditions are only partly met.

An issue affecting two cooling systems implies mechanical cooling may be down and the datacenter may be running on its load-dependent thermal buffer, but the signals do not yet show datacenter temperature approaching safe operational thresholds.

next_actions.action: Immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running, rather than assuming surge suppressors protected them.
If mechanical cooling has shut down, treat the datacenter as being on a load-dependent thermal buffer and start planning for its depletion.
Treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted.

escalate.to: facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer
escalate.reason: An issue affecting two cooling systems has been reported and engineers are assessing mitigations; mechanical cooling status is not yet confirmed, and the thermal buffer may be depleting.

not_covered: The root cause of the cooling-system issue is not yet identified in the signals; no rule addresses diagnosis of an unknown cooling fault.
The signals do not state whether storms are active or whether a utility-to-generator transfer has occurred, so R-001's full trigger conditions cannot be confirmed.
The signals do not state whether the datacenter control system is failing over or unavailable, so R-003 and R-004 cannot be applied.
The signals do not state whether datacenter temperature is approaching safe operational thresholds, so R-002's full trigger conditions cannot be confirmed.
